verdict.rationale: Bento documents natural-language alert rules that compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook, which covers every notification channel in the story. The metrics behind the alerts (cost per run, tool failure rates, drift, and regressions) are tracked out of the box, but the docs never explicitly show alert rules on cost spikes or eval-score drops. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of threshold or anomaly alerts on cost spikes and eval-score drops, alert-configuration detail beyond the FAQ, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can set alerts on error rates, cost spikes, or eval-score drops and get notified in Slack, PagerDuty, or email

citations.quote: Alerts are defined in plain natural language... Rules compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook.
Write alerts in English. Bento groups fires into incidents and judges each one real or benign
you see cost per run, tool failure rates, drift over prompt versions, and regressions across deploys out of the box.
